editorial.headline: Railways Beyond the Usual Route
editorial.standfirst: A fully foreign-open rail activity that remains registrable in Bali because it sits outside the province’s PMA moratorium trigger.
editorial.body:
KBLI 49291 covers the operation of rail services that do not form part of long-distance intercity rail or short-distance urban rail transport. Its territory includes cable railways, gondolas and other rail operations when they are outside those transport systems. The stated scope also reaches the development and provision of special railways. It is therefore a defined operational category for rail infrastructure and services with a purpose distinct from everyday intercity or city transit.

The boundaries matter. Short-distance urban tourist rail transport is outside this activity, as are cable railways, gondolas, chairlifts and similar systems when they operate as part of an amusement or recreation venue. The code is for the railway activity itself within its stated terrain, rather than a catch-all label for every rail-linked attraction or local transport service. It is open at Menengah and Besar scales, giving the category a clear commercial range without extending it beyond the scales recorded.

Nationally, the position is direct: the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That means foreign participation is open up to full ownership at the national level. The policy source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the important discipline is to keep the proposed operation faithful to the defined scope: rail services outside intercity and urban short-distance transport, including the specified cable and special-railway operations.

Bali does not reverse that national opening. The province’s permanent rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, but this activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why it is not blocked by the moratorium. A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. The result is unusually clean: a nationally open activity, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, that remains available for PMA registration in Bali because its recorded risk position falls outside the moratorium’s reach.
